text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main codebase. A common practice is creating feature branches, where each new feature or bug fix is developed separately. Once the work is finished, the branch can be merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open pull requests so others can review the changes and give feedback. This supports a clear version control workflow: create a branch, make changes, commit them, open a pull request, and merge after approval. Using branches in this way keeps the project organized and reduces the risk of conflicts.
